Note — FL2VA / L2VA PROMPT FORMAT
widgets_values:
FL2VA / L2VA PROMPT FORMAT

SCENE 1 — A TO B
Frame Gate supplies opening Frame A and the index switch supplies target Frame B. Start with the two-picture FL2VA alignment sentence: Picture 1 at 0.00 seconds and Picture 2 at 15.08 seconds. Describe the observable continuous path between them.

SCENE 2 — CONTEXT TO A
Frame Gate omits the opening image, H3 Motion Context supplies the incoming state at B, and the index switch supplies Frame A as the only explicit image. The core node therefore labels that final target <Picture 1>; use the one-picture L2VA alignment sentence at 15.08 seconds.

The switch wraps automatically: scene 1 selects frame_1 (B), scene 2 selects frame_2 (A), scene 3 would select B again.

widgets_values:
How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 15.08-second mark of the target video.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Classic Doom 1993 first-person-shooter pixel art in a World War II Market Garden scenario. Begin from the exact first-person parachute view, hands, suspension lines, canopy, airborne soldiers, bridge, river, town, sky, HUD, palette, pixel scale, and composition established by <Picture 1>. Use one uninterrupted forward-moving gameplay shot with no camera cut.

Timeline:
[0s-8s] The viewpoint descends rapidly while advancing toward the outskirts of the city. The older paratroopers descend at different depths with coherent pixel-art parallax; one soldier lands near the viewer as the bridge and river rise through frame.
[8s-10s] The player lands, the parachute collapses behind the viewpoint, and both hands pull an M1 Garand into the center of the screen. Preserve the HUD layout and first-person anatomy while the player turns toward the same dark building.
[10s-13.5s] The viewpoint runs to cover beside a friendly soldier and fires into the building. Muzzle flashes, recoil, blocky wall debris, and enemy reactions remain synchronized with the forward movement.
[13.5s-15.08s] The player pushes into the dark entrance and raises the rifle sight toward the enemy line inside. Progressively narrow every remaining difference in viewpoint, weapon position, doorway geometry, enemy spacing, HUD values, lighting, and pixel composition, landing exactly on <Picture 2> at the final frame.

overall_soundscape: Flak bursts, distant gunfire, low World War II aircraft hum, rushing air, parachute fabric, landing impacts, running footsteps, M1 Garand handling, and sharp rifle reports follow the visible action continuously. Interior reverberation becomes audible only as the viewpoint enters the building.

non_diegetic_music: A low-volume World War II-era brass-and-snare fanfare continues beneath the gameplay sounds without a new downbeat at the end.

Note — FL2V NORMAL — HOW TO USE
widgets_values:
FL2V NORMAL — A→B→A LOOP

1. Copy both bundled PNG files from example_workflows/assets into ComfyUI/input and select them in FRAME A and FRAME B.
2. Keep Current Shot.clip_index connected to the Frame Index Switch. Its frame_1 is B and frame_2 is A.
3. Keep the switch connected through Frame Gate to core last_frame. Frame Gate sends A to first_frame only for scene 1.
4. Scene 1 generates A→B with FL2VA. Scene 2 begins from H3 Motion Context at B and generates B→A with L2VA.
5. Queue and approve both scenes. Final Assemble preserves generated audio.

TIMING
Each request is 362 raw H3 frames (15.08 seconds at 24 fps). Scene 2 repeats 22 context frames, so delivery is 362 + (362 - 22) = 702 frames = 29.25 seconds.

BOUNDARIES
video_blend_frames = 0 hard-trims repeated context. The exact final A target also creates a visual endpoint suitable for looping the assembled result back to its first frame.

Note — RECOVERY / ASSEMBLE LATER
widgets_values:
The two amber recovery nodes are MUTED by default.

If all segments finished but final assembly did not, mute the main green Assemble node, enable both recovery nodes, and queue. They validate every SHA-256 checkpoint pair and assemble without rerendering the completed clips.

For an interrupted generation, leave recovery muted and set Loop Start's start_clip to the first unfinished clip.
